CVX.rationale: Chevron's fundamental health and trajectory are deteriorating sharply. Q1 2026 showed EPS of $1.11, down 44.5% YoY from $2.00, with operating cash flow collapsing 51.6% to $2.51B. The company's net margin has compressed from 7.8% a year ago to 5.9%, and ROE has fallen from 10.5% to 5.9%. The quarterly trajectory shows a clear downtrend: EPS moved from $2.00 (Q1 2025) to $1.82 (Q3 2025) to $1.45 (Q2 2025) to $1.11 (Q1 2026), with the most recent quarter being the weakest. Meanwhile, the stock is trading at a P/E of 33.2x, near the top of its 365-day range (15.3-34.8), and P/B of 1.975x is also elevated. This is a case of deteriorating fundamentals being priced at peak multiples. The valuation has nearly doubled from 15.3x P/E a year ago to 33.2x today, while earnings have nearly halved. There is no near-term fundamental catalyst to justify this re-rating; in fact, the CEO himself is warning of potential catastrophic fuel squeezes and recession risks from Middle East conflicts. Legal reserve charges, California regulatory scrutiny on refining margins, and the uncertain Hess acquisition arbitration with ExxonMobil add further downside risk. The balance sheet shows rising liabilities ($140.18B vs $130.90B in Q3 2025) while equity has declined. Oil prices at ~$97/barrel provide some support, but the company's hedging losses ($2.9B in Q1) and weak downstream margins undermine the benefit. This is a deteriorating business at an expensive valuation with multiple near-term risk catalysts.
